objective: Add organization ID to every daily OpenSearch observability index name, using global when organization ID is unavailable.

classification.reason: The index name is an operational contract consumed by an external archival process.

verified_current_behavior: The timeline collector writes all supported record kinds to <prefix>-YYYYMMDD.
The telemetry OpenSearch exporter writes logs, events, and metrics to <prefix>-<kind>-YYYYMMDD.
Both writers already receive organization ID and preserve it in indexed documents.
Telemetry readers use wildcard patterns that match both current and proposed names.
Index creation occurs through existing bulk write behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Nonzero organization IDs use unsigned base-10 formatting.
Dates remain based on occurrence time and formatted in UTC.
Organization IDs remain present inside documents.
Existing wildcard reads cover old and new layouts.
No archive lifecycle behavior is added to the application.
Focused tests and make agent-finalize pass.
No unresolved critical or major review findings remain.
non_goals: Implement or configure the archive cron.
Add retention configuration or OpenSearch lifecycle policies.
Explicitly create, archive, close, restore, or delete indexes.
Change document schemas, APIs, protobufs, databases, or connector behavior.

design.organization_segment: Unsigned base-10 organization ID, or global when OrganizationID is zero.
design.date_source: Existing record occurrence time behavior, with current UTC time used when occurrence time is zero.
design.implementation: Change only the existing private index-name functions and their call sites.
design.cron_contract: The external cron parses relative to exact configured prefixes and supports old and new layouts during rollout.

principle_decisions.kiss: Modify only the two existing OpenSearch writers and their focused tests.
principle_decisions.yagni: Do not add shared packages, new configuration, lifecycle workers, connector APIs, policies, templates, or migrations.
principle_decisions.single_source_of_truth: Each existing writer remains the owner of its established prefix and record-kind naming.
principle_decisions.compatibility: Preserve document fields, bulk behavior, custom prefixes, UTC dates, wildcard reads, and all existing indexes.
principle_decisions.failure_safety: Use global instead of dropping records when organization context is missing.
principle_decisions.rollback: Roll back the application binary. Both layouts remain readable through existing wildcard patterns.

risks.risk: Organization-by-day routing increases the number of indexes and shards.
risks.disposition: Accepted as an operational consequence of organization-specific archival. Capacity monitoring remains an operator responsibility.

risks.risk: Custom prefixes can contain hyphens or numeric tokens.
risks.disposition: The archive cron must strip the exact configured prefix before parsing organization and date suffixes.

risks.risk: Records without organization context share the global index.
risks.disposition: Accepted to preserve observability delivery. The global index has its own cron handling.

risks.risk: Late records can write to an old date index.
risks.disposition: Existing occurrence-time routing is preserved. Repeated archival handling remains owned by the external cron.

rollout: Update the external cron to recognize old and new layouts using exact configured prefixes.
Verify index names and matching document organization IDs.
Verify existing wildcard reads and dashboards.
